# A window under an `if` that reads state comes and goes with it wherever the
# window is a component: a node in a render slot on gtk4 and fyne, and a node
# in a view re-rendered whole on bubbletea and android. html renders a window
# as the builtin it is marked, a document written once, so there it is refused
# at the window rather than emitted as if the `if` were not there.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html app.sngl
stderr 'app.sngl:10:14: a window under an `if` that reads state is created and destroyed with it, which html cannot do'

sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea -o tea only.sngl
sngl generate --lang kotlin --platform android -o droid only.sngl

# A condition that reads no state is not a lifetime, and builds anywhere.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html2 const.sngl

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var details = false

ui.window #main(title="Main") {
    ui.button(text="Details", @click { details = !details })
}

if details {
    ui.window(title="Load") {
        ui.text(value="load")
    }
}
-- const.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

const wide = true

ui.window #main(title="Main") {
    ui.text(value="main")
}

if wide {
    ui.window(title="Wide", href="/wide.html") {
        ui.text(value="wide")
    }
}
-- only.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var details = true

if details {
    ui.window(title="Load", @closed {
        details = false
    }) {
        ui.text(value="load")
    }
}
